items.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002
items.q: there’s a great quote from Duke Ellington

ctx.x: Yeah I believe so. And it seems like it’s an innovation in a sense when you’re bringing all those elements together because I’ve often wondered if it’s constantly getting harder for people to become innovators.

It’s a good question. Well it gets back again to industry stuff because you know in the 80s and 90s you had this term neoclassism thrown around a lot when it came to jazz. And they would often associate Wynton Marsalis with well he’s a neoclassicist because he’s playing in the style of Miles or the style of Louis or whatever. I mean now the musicians never thought, we never sat around talking, “Yeah you know what? I’m going to play something in the neoclassicist style.” You know? We never think that way. We’re…

Nobel Peace Prize in 1969 or something like that. And when he was rejected for it and someone told him about it and Duke said, “Well I guess I wasn’t supposed to be too famous too soon. And here’s a guy who had been around for 50 years at that point and had already left an amazing legacy. And that just gives you a sense of where he was. He wasn’t thinking about accolades or accomplishments. And of course now we know him to be probably one of the greatest innovators if not the greatest of twentieth century music…
